note: PSNL ran up to a ~$17.06 intraday high while it had zero stop protection (startTrailing() race bug, see CLAUDE.md's Scheduling/EOD sections and orderManager.ts's cancelStopIfLive) — a working trailing stop (peak - $0.15 trailingStopAmount) should have exited around $16.91. Instead there was no stop resting at all during that run-up; price pulled back and the position was still open afterward. Approximate cost: ~$0.26-0.41/share x 300 shares left on the table versus a correctly-trailed exit, on top of the unprotected-risk exposure itself. The bug is now fixed (see orderManager.ts startTrailing/cancelStopIfLive/placeFallbackBreakevenStop), but this specific missed exit is not recoverable and won't show up in trades.jsonl's own numbers since no exit was ever logged at the peak.

A duplicate backup schedule run (id 33540027294) slipped past both EOD guards (see CLAUDE.md's 2026-09-01 entry) and was manually cancelled via 'gh run cancel' ~19:15 UTC once caught. The cancellation did NOT take effect promptly -- GitHub kept the job running on the old pre-fix code for another 4h13m, and at 19:55:01 UTC it placed a real live entry: MSTZ, 300 sh, filled at 5.41, stop resting at 5.26 (stop order_id/client_order_id Q5HES80NHRCUCBEC624NS58UPA / 26ff09e603034d0bbde80b3835fd9271, confirmed via checkPositions.ts). GitHub finally force-killed the job at 23:28:23 UTC, mid-git-rebase during its own commit step, which then failed -- so this entry_placed event never made it into trades.jsonl. The position is real on the broker's side; this note exists because the log doesn't know about it. Decision: left open overnight, unmanaged but protected by its own resting stop -- tomorrow's normal session reconcile() will pick it up and manage it forward, the same proven path used for any other restart-with-open-position case. Bigger lesson: 'gh run cancel' is NOT a reliable immediate stop for a live trading job -- it can keep running for hours afterward. Going forward this specific scenario (a queued run starting past the 3:15pm ET EOD target) is closed by the isPastEodCloseTime() fix already shipped the same day -- this incident only happened because this particular run had already checked out the code from before that fix.

A backup 'schedule' run (GitHub Actions run id 34260009882, event=schedule) queued behind the concurrency lock and started executing right as the primary session's EOD close finished (~19:15:34 UTC). It correctly detected isPastEodCloseTime() and ran its own EOD close before ever going live -- during reconcile() it found a real broker-side SID position (qty=300, cost basis 1.29, phase=HARD_STOP, stopTracked=false) that has NO entry_placed anywhere in trades.jsonl (last logged SID activity was the 2026-09-03 round trip). It closed the position (logged locally as exit_filled SID), but the job's own commit-back step then hit a git rebase conflict against the primary session's just-pushed commit (both trades.jsonl and watchlist.json conflicted) and errored out (exit code 1) without resolving -- so neither the original entry_placed for this SID position nor this exit_filled ever reached the repo. Confirmed via checkPositions.ts (run manually 2026-09-08 ~20:15 UTC) that the broker is currently flat: zero open positions, zero open orders -- so there is no live risk, only a gap in the historical record. Origin of the untracked SID entry itself is unknown (no entry_placed for it exists in any commit); likely lost the same way during an earlier merge-conflicted commit sometime between 2026-09-04 and today. Same underlying failure mode as the 2026-09-01 gh-run-cancel incident: a broker-side fill can outlive a failed commit step, silently diverging trades.jsonl from reality. Not yet fixed structurally -- worth considering a retry-on-conflict (or fetch+merge before commit, not rebase) in the workflow's commit-back step if this recurs.
